purpose: Deucravacitinib is used to treat adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, which is a skin condition that causes red, scaly, itchy patches on the skin. It is used when other treatments like creams or light therapy have not worked well enough. This medication helps calm the skin and reduce flare-ups.
how_it_works: Your immune system can sometimes overreact and attack your own skin, causing the red, scaly patches seen in psoriasis. Deucravacitinib works by blocking a specific protein in your immune system called TYK2, which acts like a switch that turns on inflammation. By blocking this switch, the medication helps turn down the overactive immune response and gives your skin a chance to heal.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upper respiratory infections like the common cold, cold sores or mouth sores (herpes simplex), acne, folliculitis (small pimples around hair follicles), and elevated levels of certain fats in your blood called triglycerides. Some people also notice mild rashes or skin reactions.
warnings: Before starting this medication, tell your doctor if you have any infections, as deucravacitinib can lower your immune response and make it harder to fight infections. Let your doctor know if you have a history of tuberculosis (TB), hepatitis B or C, or any cancer. You should be up to date on your vaccinations before starting treatment. Avoid live vaccines while taking this medication. It is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding, so talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 6 mg taken by mouth once daily, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you start feeling better.
